# Isleta 2.0.0
The notch became something you can browse. Three pages — your day, your music, the weather — turned with a two-finger swipe, with everything that arrives on its own taking the stage in front of them. Now in German, French and Spanish.
## New
- **Three pages, and a swipe between them.** Today, Music and Weather. Swipe two fingers across an open island to turn the page. They wrap, so there is no end to walk into. - **Your day, in the notch.** What is next in your calendar, with a button that joins the meeting. Choose which calendars count in Settings. - **The weather where you are.** Today's high and low, what it feels like, and the chance of rain for the next few days. Use your location, or type a city and pick it from the list. - **When it's raining, it rains in the island.** The drops land on its bottom edge. Snow falls too, and both stop if you have asked macOS to reduce motion. - **A music page that shows the whole track.** Long titles scroll and then settle, the album artwork lends the island its color, and the audio format shows as a small badge. - **Up Next.** The queue your player is working through, the output device, favorite and playback speed. Double-click anything in the list to play it. - **Drop files on the island to convert them.** Images, images to PDF, video, audio, Word, RTF, HTML, spreadsheets and presentations. Search the shelf, preview with Space, and look back through everything Isleta has made for you. - **Drop audio or video to transcribe it.** The text lands beside the original. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is asked of you. - **Copy Link** puts a shareable iCloud link on your clipboard. For files outside iCloud Drive it offers AirDrop instead. - **Isleta can answer your volume and brightness keys.** Turn it on under Sources and the island replaces macOS's own HUD rather than sitting beside it. Volume and brightness are separate switches, both off until you turn them on. - **A card on the lock screen** showing what is playing. It arrives when the Mac locks and leaves the moment you unlock it. Off until you turn it on. - **AirPods and other Bluetooth devices announce themselves** when they connect, with the battery level if the device reports one. - **Battery, calls and timers.** The charger going in and out, a low battery, Low Power Mode, a call in progress with how long it has been going, and timers you start in Clock. - **A first run that asks once.** Eight short screens, five of them permissions — accessibility, music, calendar, weather and devices — each showing what the permission is for, and which button to press, before it asks. Skip any of them and the rest of Isleta still works. - **A list of apps the island stays out of entirely**, for full-screen video or a presentation. - **Keyboard shortcuts** for opening the island and showing your day, under General. Opening the island ships bound to ⌃⌥⌘I, because Isleta has no Dock icon and its menu bar item can be hidden; showing your day is unassigned until you assign it. - **Quick actions in the menu bar** for whatever is on the island right now. The icon can be hidden; Quit and Open Setup Guide live in About as well. - **German, French and Spanish**, following your Mac's language.
## Improved
- **Settings is a much smaller place.** Four panes instead of seven, and roughly a third as many controls. What went were the settings asking you a question Isleta can answer for itself. - **The island is black in a real notch and glass where it floats**, and no longer asks you to choose. It was never a matter of taste, so it is no longer a setting. - **The whole island moves as one.** Its width, height and corners travel together, so opening it reads as a single motion rather than two. - **Reduce motion, reduce transparency and increase contrast are honored throughout.**
## Fixed
- **Settings opens on the desktop you are looking at**, rather than the one you last opened it on. Opening Settings now closes the island. - **Playing music costs a fraction of what it did.** A playing track is now about as light as a quiet island. - **Closing Up Next gives the island its height back.** The ✕ used to leave it tall. - **AirPods connecting no longer hangs Isleta at launch.**
## Removed
- **Notifications, and everything built on them** — banners in the island, grouping, quick reply, per-app rules, and the list of the ones you missed. macOS offers no way to hide its own banner short of clearing the notification outright, so Isleta was only ever a second banner beside Apple's, announcing something already on your screen. - **The app switcher.** ⌘⇥ already moves between apps, and Isleta's version wanted Screen Recording to do the same job with worse pictures. Screen Recording is no longer requested at all. - **The player bar**, the floating transport for displays the island does not reach. The island is the product; a second surface was a different one. - **Downloads, mounted disks and app updates.** Each announced something the Finder, the Dock or the app itself had already said. - **The month grid.** Clicking the date opened a wall planner. What you ask a notch is what is next.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac without one gets a floating island on the main display.
## Known limitations
- **You cannot see who is calling.** macOS does not let apps outside Apple read that, or answer for you. Isleta shows that a call is happening and nothing more. - **Weather needs your location, or a city you type.** Isleta asks for neither until you use it. - **A connected device's battery is read once, when it connects.** It does not tick down as you wear them, and most non-Apple headphones report no level at all. - **A timer started by Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center can take a few seconds to appear.** One started by hand in Clock is there immediately. - **Replacing the system HUDs is off until you turn it on, and it needs Accessibility.** Quitting Isleta hands your keys straight back; if Isleta is force-quit, the system HUD stays out of the way until Isleta next starts. Brightness covers the built-in display only. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a floating island can sit over the middle of the space labels.

# Isleta 1.3.1
Two ways into Settings that no longer depend on the menu bar icon — the gear is on every open island now, and Export Logs… is inside Settings itself — and a notification list that opens smoothly.
## Improved
- **The gear is on every open island.** It used to appear only when there was something else to switch to, so an island with music playing and nothing waiting had no way into Settings at all. Open any island and rest the pointer on it — the row along the bottom has the gear in it, the same as when notifications are being held. - **Opening the notification list is smoother.** With a full list the island used to stutter as it grew to fit it. Only the rows you can see are built now, and most of that stutter is gone in both directions. - **Export Logs… is in Settings ▸ About.** It is the one thing you are asked for in a bug report, and it used to live only behind the menu bar icon, which you can now hide. It writes the same single file, wherever you choose to save it — no notification text, track titles or file names in it.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac with none gets a synthesized island on the primary display.
## Known limitations
- **The battery is a snapshot, not a readout.** It is read once, when the device connects, and the island goes a few seconds later. It does not tick down while you wear them — macOS gives no signal when the level changes, and Isleta will not poll for one. - **Third-party headphones may show no battery.** Most non-Apple devices do not report a level to macOS at all. They still get their moment in the notch, with no ring beside them. - **A burst of notifications opens the island once for each.** The list is where the ones you missed go; grouping them as they arrive is a later release's job. - **A timer started by Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center can take a few seconds to appear.** One started by hand in Clock is there immediately; macOS gives no signal for the others, and Isleta will not poll for them. - **The keyboard backlight HUD can appear when the room light changes.** macOS adjusts the backlight for ambient light on its own, and does not say whether a change came from you or from the room. Isleta ignores the idle fade, which is the common case, but cannot tell the other two apart. Turn off “Adjust keyboard brightness in low light” if it bothers you. - **Apple's own HUDs and banners are not replaced.** Isleta shows its own alongside them. For notifications the only way to hide Apple's banner is the one the system treats as you clearing the notification outright, which would empty your Notification Center as the price of a tidier screen. Not a trade Isleta will make for you. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a synthesized island can cover the centre of the space labels. - **Playing music costs more than it should.** About 7.7% CPU against an internal 4% budget for an animating island, and a 250–290 MB footprint against a 60 MB one. It is not a leak: resident memory is flat and plateaus rather than climbing. - **Bluetooth headphones cost something at idle.** With AirPods connected, Isleta sits at about 0.5% of a core with nothing on stage, against an internal 0.3% budget; with none connected it measures 0.02%. It is under investigation and it is not the AirPods *feature* — switching that source off does not move the figure, and neither the quiet island nor the AirPods moment adds a timer of its own.

# Isleta 1.3.0
Clicking the island when nothing is playing now opens it, onto the two things it always has: the notifications you missed, and Settings. AirPods say hello when you put them in. And notifications wear the icon of the app that sent them, scroll, and open that app when you click one.
## New
- **Brightness HUDs, for the display and the keyboard.** Change either and the island shows the level, the same way it already did for volume — the glyph in one sliver, the bar in the other. It arrives alongside Apple's own HUD rather than replacing it.
Both were listed as impossible in the last four releases. Neither is: macOS publishes both levels and announces every change, just not through the APIs everyone reaches for first. Isleta reads them without asking for any permission, and stays completely idle between changes.
- **An empty island opens instead of refusing.** Click the notch on a quiet Mac and the island opens onto two buttons — Notifications and Settings — and nothing else. It is as short as an open island can be, and it closes the way any other does. - **Settings is one click from the notch.** No shortcut to remember and no menu bar icon needed, which matters most if you have hidden the icon. - **AirPods show up in the notch when they connect.** Take them out of the case and the island shows the AirPods themselves beside a ring of how much charge is left, for a few seconds, then goes. It works for AirPods, AirPods Pro, AirPods Max, Beats, and any other Bluetooth headphones or speaker — the ones Apple makes get their own picture, everything else gets a generic pair. The ring turns amber below 20%, so a pair that will not last the afternoon says so. Isleta asks for Bluetooth access the first time it starts — that is what lets it hear a device arrive — and the whole thing can be switched off in Settings ▸ Sources. - **Notifications wear the icon of the app that sent them.** Mail, Messages, Calendar, Slack — whatever posted it, in the island and in the list, in place of the bell. The bell is still what you get for an app Isleta cannot find on the disk. - **Clicking a notification opens the app it came from.** It works the way clicking a banner does: the app comes forward, the row goes, and the island closes behind it. Your Notification Center copy is left alone — Isleta reads that list, it does not clear it for you.
## Improved
- **The notification list no longer disappears when you click something else.** Clicking back into the window you were working in used to take the list away mid-read. It now stays until you dismiss it — with **Clear All**, with the **✕** beside it, or with Escape. - **Clear All empties the list and closes the island** in one go, rather than leaving you looking at "Nothing recent". - **The Notifications button says how many are new**, so a quiet island still tells you whether anything happened while you were away. - **The notification list scrolls.** All twenty it keeps are reachable now, not just the five that fit — two fingers on the notch move the list, and a slim indicator down the edge says where in it you are. While the list is open that flick scrolls rather than closing the island; Clear All, the ✕ and Escape are still the ways out. - **A notification arriving while you are reading brings the list back to the top**, so you watch it land instead of finding the rows rearranged under you.
## Fixed
- **The island no longer reopens at the wrong size after reading notifications.** Closing the list and opening the island again could leave it as tall as the list had been, with far less in it.
- **Two ear pieces are reported as the lower of the two.** If one bud is at 50% and the other at 100%, the ring shows 50 — the one that runs out first is the one worth knowing about, and it is what Apple's own menu shows.
